messages:
mike-support: Hey team — customer flagged missing CloudTrail objects in S3 after our recent KMS key rotation. They say audit logs older than 30d disappeared. Ticket #12345. Any ideas?

oncall-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-12345. Pager notified. :rotating_light:

jamie-ops: which bucket + key alias? do we have timeline of the rotation?

mike-support: bucket: redwood-audit-prod-logs, key alias: alias/ci-audit-2023 -> rotated 2026-02-18 02:14 UTC. first missing object appears 2026-03-03. customer uses SSE-KMS via PutObject.

tessa-sec: quick checklist: 1) confirm S3 lifecycle didn't delete (check bucket lifecycle, versioning), 2) check KMS key policy & grants allowed decrypt/generateDataKey for CloudTrail service principal and for whoever wrote objects, 3) confirm encryption context preserved on PutObject if using client-side encryption or proxy.

jen-sre: to inspect, run:
```
aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket redwood-audit-prod-logs
aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket redwood-audit-prod-logs
aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name redwood-audit-trail
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/ci-audit-2023
```

Also check CloudTrail delivery status in console for PutObject failures.

mike-support: customer provided a snippet from their side showing 403 from S3 PutObject at time of rotation window — they assumed we dropped objects. They also saw KMS Decrypt errors in our proxy logs: "AccessDeniedException: EncryptionContextMismatch".

tessa-sec: EncryptionContextMismatch suggests the ciphertext had a different encryption context than what the requester provided to Decrypt or that context was dropped by the proxy. If objects were re-encrypted or keys rotated, older objects still decryptable if KMS grants/policies allow decrypt with old CMK or key material via re-encrypt flow. Did we perform an alias swap vs key rekey? Alias swap is fine; key rotation (new CMK) without re-encrypt will still allow decrypt if key still exists and policy allows.

jamie-ops: action items for support: a) ask customer for a sample object key + full S3 PutObject response headers b) ask for the exact ErrorId and timestamp of their 403 c) we should grep our proxy logs for KMS Decrypt errors around that timestamp and include request IDs.

jen-sre: immediate mitigation: disable lifecycle transitions for that prefix and enable versioning if not set; copy existing objects to a staging bucket encrypted with a known-working CMK to preserve for compliance. long-term: confirm CloudTrail -> S3 uses SSE-KMS with the correct KMS key and that CloudTrail has permissions to use KMS key via key policy `{"Principal":{"Service":"cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"}}` and Sts conditions if cross-account.

mike-support: I can ask the customer for object key and timestamp. If we find EncryptionContextMismatch on our side, what's the usual cause in our infra?

tessa-sec: common: proxies that strip headers, custom SDKs that omit x-amz-server-side-encryption-context, or double-encryption where client-supplied context != server expectations. Also misconfigured kms:Decrypt condition in key policy that requires specific encryption context value.

jamie-ops: repro steps for infra team:
```
# simulate PutObject with SSE-KMS and encryption context
aws s3api put-object --bucket redwood-audit-prod-logs --key test-ctx.json --body sample.json --server-side-encryption aws:kms --ssekms-key-id alias/ci-audit-2023 --metadata '{"x-amz-server-side-encryption-context":"env=prod"}'
# then try decrypt via kms
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://cipher.bin --encryption-context '{"env":"prod"}' --key-id alias/ci-audit-2023
```
If the proxy rewrites or strips the context the decrypt will fail with EncryptionContextMismatch.

jen-sre: file note: also check CloudTrail's own S3 PutObject uses CloudTrail service principal; it should not send encryption context unless configured. If the customer used client-side context, there can be mismatch.

mike-support: thanks. I'll get object key + headers and share. marking P0 until we confirm retention/restore path. :thumbsup:
